analysis.title: AI's Moment Of Truth / France Ratings Hold / Brazil's Lula Wins / Central Bank Week
key_insights: October's AI selloff reads as structural rather than forced selling like July's: investors question whether monetization and AI demand can keep pace with the infrastructure build given the repricing in funding costs.

This week's hyperscaler results are the test. Strong Azure/AWS/Google Cloud, capacity-constrained demand and intact capex would mean the AI demand story is unchanged. Slowing cloud growth alongside higher capex would validate the bear case that spending is ahead of monetization.

The desk says price action over the next seven days will likely dictate price action for the next seven weeks. The large increase in shorts leaves the market vulnerable to a squeeze, while breaks of technical supports would shift the market to broad-based selling.

Moody's kept France at Aa3 (negative outlook), one notch above Fitch and S&P. The rating assumes a deficit-reducing 2027 budget is adopted and that financing costs and social tensions ease in the next few months. French assets may get relief on Monday.

Lula was re-elected for a fourth term with 51.76% vs 48.24% for Flavio Bolsonaro. The desk expects a significant repricing of Brazilian assets Monday, with USDBRL potentially at 5.3. EM strategist Roque Montero sees USDBRL at 5.5-5.6 by end-2026, a 100-150bp rise in rates and a 10-15% equity correction.
US-Iran rhetoric eased and Brent fell 1.8% toward $114/bbl after a six-month high last week. WTI fell about 2% toward $101/bbl. Brent's 14-day RSI topped 74 on Friday.

UBS Economics expects a 25bp RBNZ hike on Oct. 27, an FOMC skip and 25bp BoC hike on Oct. 28, and ECB and BoJ holds on Oct. 29 and Oct. 30. FX bias is long AUDUSD, short USDSEK and EURSEK, and reduce short USDCAD near 1.40. The rates view is to keep 2y UST receivers.

UBS Economics expects a hawkish FOMC hold Wednesday. Chair Warsh is expected to stress that inflation remains elevated. Hikes in December and January remain the base case. Underlying inflation is near 3% and Q3 GDP is projected at 3.6% saar.
The October BoJ prices 0.5bp of a hike. The desk favours paying the December/January BoJ at +6.5, steepening 1s2s TONAR at +24bp, and being paid JPY vs EUR in cross-currency basis.

China's Fifth Plenum (Monday to Thursday) is unlikely to deliver a major policy package. The next policy window is the NPC Standing Committee meeting on Nov. 2-6. The team expects RMB to strengthen with USDCNY toward 6.60 by year-end.
RBA Chief Economist Hunter said rates may need to rise again after the cash rate reached 4.6%. UBS Economics sees another 25bp hike, most likely in November.
UK long-end flattening looks crowded and near fair value. The desk prefers long-end steepeners and shorter-dated flatteners or 2s5s30s structures.

About 25% of S&P market cap has reported Q3: 78% beat, revenue is up 12.5% and earnings are tracking +31% y/y. Hedge funds are selling AI winners and momentum. Long exposure fell from the 90th to the 15th percentile since September, shorts rose from the 15th to the 80th, and equity long/short funds are down 7% in October.

UBS's derivatives strategist keeps a medium-term bullish view. Long-duration capital (retail, retirement, foreign) drives the destination while systematic and hedge fund strategies drive short-term volatility, so deleveraging is more likely a temporary dislocation than a trend reversal.

UBS equity strategy sees AI credit stress as concentrated, not broad. Hyperscaler yield increases are mostly explained by Treasury yields (Oracle excepted) and neoclouds are only 5-7% of expected AI datacentre capex. A 15% ROIC by 2031 on $7.7trn of 2026-30 hyperscaler spend needs $1trn of incremental EBIT and about $3.4trn of revenue.

KOSPI 12m forward P/E fell to 4.2x. SK Hynix plans a special dividend of about KRW16trn (~USD12bn) and reports Wednesday, with Samsung Thursday. The desk has a sell skew in Japan, Hong Kong and Korea and is a net seller of Technology and Financials.

Trump and Hassett said a US-Canada tariff deal could come soon. Ukraine agreed to trilateral talks with the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November, but Moscow has not agreed to take part.
EMEA flows: European AI winners fell over 8% and defensives rose. APAC's selloff looked like a confidence shock on thin liquidity, with Korean foreign selling slowing.

FX and metals levels: EURUSD resistance is 1.1260 and 1.1280-1.1285 with support near 1.1160, and the stance is bearish. The desk prefers selling gold rallies toward 4025-4035 with downside levels at 3975 and 3950-3955. In USDPHP the desk likes staying paid in the curve.

sector_views.rationale: The desk is a net seller of Technology and Financials in Asia. Hedge funds are unwinding AI winners and momentum, though UBS strategists see the AI credit stress as contained.
Energy and software (particularly cybersecurity) led US equity outperformers Friday, and Energy and Technology are the only sectors outpacing S&P earnings growth.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 earnings, with about 25% of market cap reported: 78% of companies beat expectations, revenue is growing 12.5% and earnings are tracking 31% higher y/y.
SK Hynix reports Wednesday and Samsung Electronics Thursday. SK Hynix plans a special dividend of about KRW16trn (~USD12bn), per Dong-A Ilbo.
Hyperscaler results this week (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud growth and capex plans) are the focus for the AI complex including Nvidia and Micron.

Iran will host security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey. CENTCOM highlighted robust crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
Brazil: Lula won a fourth term. Flavio Bolsonaro requested annulment of the runoff, alleging the Supreme Court changed rules mid-vote.
France: protests continued without serious incidents and Moody's held the rating.
Ukraine agreed to trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November. Zelenskiy asked for security guarantees and 10 years of funding for the army.
US-Canada tariff dispute: Trump said it would be settled 'pretty soon' and Hassett said talks are 'very close'.
China's Fifth Plenum runs Monday to Thursday, with the NPC Standing Committee meeting on Nov. 2-6 next.

tension_points.bull_case: If Azure/AWS/Google Cloud stay strong, demand stays capacity constrained and capex plans hold, the AI demand story is unchanged and the move was about positioning and funding. Credit stress is concentrated and Treasury yields explain most of the rise in hyperscaler yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Slowing cloud growth alongside another leg higher in capex would validate the view that infrastructure spending is getting ahead of monetization. A 15% ROIC by 2031 needs $1trn of incremental EBIT and about $3.4trn of revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowing cloud growth alongside higher capex in this week's hyperscaler results would invalidate the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Long-duration capital from retail, retirement and foreign investors supports buy-the-dip demand and V-shaped recoveries, and Q3 earnings are strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Technical support breaks would move the market from rotation to broad-based selling, and short exposure is at the 80th percentile.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Labor-market weakness, prolonged inflation, geopolitical shocks or fading US exceptionalism that erode capital persistence.
